chunks: From him, from Salih ibn Khallad and Ubays ibn Hasham, from Thabit, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a village that has outlying farms, date palms, crops, gardens, and orchards; I buy its produce. He said, 'There is no objection.'

key_terms.أَرْحَاءٌ: Outlying farms or districts surrounding a city
key_terms.أَرْطَابٌ: Orchards or groves of fruit trees
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy the future produce of a mixed agricultural village in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the permissibility of purchasing the future produce (*ghallah*) of a comprehensive agricultural estate, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that such transactions are valid provided the assets are clearly defined. It highlights the practical application of contract law in agrarian societies, where the Imam (peace be upon him) validates the sale of mixed yields from diverse sources like palms, crops, and gardens as a single unit.
